subject: sql
text: List the name and salary of all employees who work in Pune, ordered by name.
explanation: Filter rows with WHERE, then sort with ORDER BY.

sql.referenceQuery: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE city = 'Pune' ORDER BY name;

subject: sql
text: List the distinct, non-NULL cities where employees are based, in alphabetical order.
explanation: DISTINCT removes duplicates. NULL must be tested with IS NOT NULL, never "<> NULL".

sql.referenceQuery: SELECT DISTINCT city FROM employees WHERE city IS NOT NULL ORDER BY city;

subject: sql
text: Return the total payroll (sum of salaries) and the average salary rounded to 2 decimals, in one row.
explanation: Aggregate functions collapse all rows into one when there is no GROUP BY.

sql.referenceQuery: SELECT SUM(salary), ROUND(AVG(salary), 2) FROM employees;

subject: sql
text: For each dept_id, show the number of employees. Order by dept_id.
explanation: GROUP BY forms one group per dept_id; COUNT(*) counts rows in each.

sql.referenceQuery: SELECT dept_id, COUNT(*) FROM employees GROUP BY dept_id ORDER BY dept_id;

subject: sql
text: Show department names whose average salary is above 60000, with the average rounded to 2 decimals. Order by department name.
explanation: Join to get names, group by department, and use HAVING (not WHERE) to filter on an aggregate.

sql.referenceQuery: SELECT d.dept_name, ROUND(AVG(e.salary), 2) FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id GROUP BY d.dept_name HAVING AVG(e.salary) > 60000 ORDER BY d.dept_name;

subject: sql
text: List each employee name with their department name, ordered by employee name.
explanation: INNER JOIN keeps only rows that match on dept_id.

sql.referenceQuery: SELECT e.name, d.dept_name FROM employees e INNER JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id ORDER BY e.name;

subject: sql
text: List every department with its number of employees, including departments with none. Order by department name.
explanation: LEFT JOIN keeps departments with no employees. COUNT(e.emp_id) ignores the NULLs, giving 0.

sql.referenceQuery: SELECT d.dept_name, COUNT(e.emp_id) FROM departments d LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id GROUP BY d.dept_id, d.dept_name ORDER BY d.dept_name;

subject: sql
text: List each employee with their manager's name (NULL if none), ordered by employee name.
explanation: Join the table to itself using manager_id = emp_id; LEFT JOIN retains the top manager.

sql.referenceQuery: SELECT e.name, m.name FROM employees e LEFT JOIN employees m ON e.manager_id = m.emp_id ORDER BY e.name;

subject: sql
text: Find the names of employees who earn more than the company average salary, ordered by name.
explanation: A scalar subquery computes the average once; compare each salary with it.

sql.referenceQuery: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees) ORDER BY name;

subject: sql
text: Find employees who earn more than the average salary of their own department. Return name, ordered by name.
explanation: The inner query references the outer row (e.dept_id), so it is re-evaluated per employee.

sql.referenceQuery: SELECT e.name FROM employees e WHERE e.salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees WHERE dept_id = e.dept_id) ORDER BY e.name;

subject: sql
text: Label each employee's salary band: "High" if salary >= 80000, "Mid" if >= 50000, otherwise "Low". Return name and band, ordered by name.
explanation: CASE evaluates conditions top to bottom and returns the first match.

sql.referenceQuery: SELECT name, CASE WHEN salary >= 80000 THEN 'High' WHEN salary >= 50000 THEN 'Mid' ELSE 'Low' END FROM employees ORDER BY name;

columns: CASE WHEN salary >= 80000 THEN 'High' WHEN salary >= 50000 THEN 'Mid' ELSE 'Low' END

subject: sql
text: Show each employee name with their city, replacing a missing city with "Unknown". Order by name.
explanation: COALESCE returns its first non-NULL argument.

sql.referenceQuery: SELECT name, COALESCE(city, 'Unknown') FROM employees ORDER BY name;

subject: sql
text: List names (in UPPER case) of employees hired in 2022, ordered by name.
explanation: strftime extracts the year from an ISO date string in SQLite.

sql.referenceQuery: SELECT UPPER(name) FROM employees WHERE strftime('%Y', hire_date) = '2022' ORDER BY name;

subject: sql
text: Find email addresses that appear more than once in employees, with their counts.
explanation: Group by the column and keep groups with more than one row.

sql.referenceQuery: SELECT email, COUNT(*) FROM employees GROUP BY email HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

subject: sql
text: Find the second-highest distinct salary.
explanation: The highest salary below the overall maximum is the second highest. Using DISTINCT semantics avoids ties.

sql.referenceQuery: SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees);

subject: sql
text: Find the 3rd-highest distinct salary.
explanation: Take distinct salaries in descending order and skip two (OFFSET 2).

sql.referenceQuery: SELECT salary FROM (SELECT DISTINCT salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 2);

subject: sql
text: For each employee show name, dept_id and their salary rank within the department using RANK (highest salary = 1). Order by dept_id, rank, name.
explanation: PARTITION BY restarts ranking in each department. RANK gives ties the same rank and skips the next numbers.

sql.referenceQuery: SELECT name, dept_id, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY dept_id ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rnk FROM employees ORDER BY dept_id, rnk, name;

subject: sql
text: Using a CTE of total salary per department, list department ids whose total is greater than the average of those totals. Order by dept_id.
explanation: The CTE names an intermediate result so it can be reused twice.

sql.referenceQuery: WITH t AS (SELECT dept_id, SUM(salary) AS total FROM employees GROUP BY dept_id) SELECT dept_id FROM t WHERE total > (SELECT AVG(total) FROM t) ORDER BY dept_id;

subject: sql
text: List the names of customers who have never placed an order, ordered by name.
explanation: After a LEFT JOIN, customers without orders have NULL order columns.

sql.referenceQuery: SELECT c.name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.cust_id = c.cust_id WHERE o.order_id IS NULL ORDER BY c.name;

subject: sql
text: Which customer has the highest total of delivered orders? Return the name and total.
explanation: Filter to delivered, aggregate per customer, sort descending and keep one row.

sql.referenceQuery: SELECT c.name, SUM(o.amount) AS total FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.cust_id = c.cust_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY c.cust_id, c.name ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 1;

subject: sql
text: Show order_id, amount and the running total of amount ordered by order_id.
explanation: SUM() OVER (ORDER BY …) accumulates from the first row to the current one.

sql.referenceQuery: SELECT order_id, amount, SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY order_id) AS running FROM orders ORDER BY order_id;

subject: sql
text: For each department that has employees, return the dept_name and the highest salary in it. Order by dept_name.
explanation: Group employees by department and take MAX(salary).

sql.referenceQuery: SELECT d.dept_name, MAX(e.salary) FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id GROUP BY d.dept_id, d.dept_name ORDER BY d.dept_name;
